A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAE classification and transferability study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across the revised pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, multilingual transfer, multimodal transfer, and behavioral prediction results, including pooling and width analyses and appendix performance tables.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including Figures 3–15 and the classification and feature-overlap tables.

M1.justification: The pretrained SAE extraction, pooling, binarization, and logistic-regression pipeline is retained. Appendix A.1 explains existing selectors; the L2 regularization and ReLU disclosures do not establish changes to the implemented method.

E1.justification: Table 2 and the retained experiments cover the same classification datasets, languages, vision tasks, and QA scenarios. Section 4's new description of a three-binary-task focus conflicts with the retained broader coverage; it does not establish dataset removal. The new MTEB citation adds no demonstrated evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain TF-IDF, hidden-state probes, and Mean-Diff top-N comparisons. The added discussion of sparsity methods and citations does not introduce an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The reported model configurations, layers, widths, pooling settings, binarization threshold, five-fold cross-validation, and transfer procedures remain unchanged. L2 regularization and training-set feature-selection details are newly disclosed settings, rather than explicit protocol revisions.

E4.justification: The layer, width, pooling, binarization, sampling-rate, feature-overlap, and context-manipulation analyses are retained. Section 8's proposed covariate, subpopulation, and temporal-shift evaluations are future work, not newly conducted robustness tests.

E5.justification: There are no added run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical tests. Figure 5 retains its mean, standard-deviation, and interquartile-range description. The new statement about lower variance changes the reported finding, not the uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Section 5.2 newly states that Mean-Diff has higher average F1 and lower variance, qualifying v1's unfavorable characterization using the retained Figure 5. This changes qualitative result reporting. The numerical tables and plotted results are otherwise retained; Table 5 only rounds three-decimal values to two decimals.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.1 explicitly defines the token-level activation mask and the dataset-level selection score as the absolute difference between class-conditional mean activations. These add formal specificity to previously described selectors. The original summation and binarization equations remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about SAE classification performance, cross-lingual and multimodal transfer, and smaller-model oversight of larger models.

C2.justification: v2 adds model and baseline-selection rationales, qualifies computational savings as theoretical, recommends Mean-Diff when average performance and stability matter, and discusses task-dependent disagreement with prior work. The limitations now distinguish domain-independent structure from domain-specific correlations and outline concrete distribution-shift questions.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 clarifies token-wise selection versus supervised selection over the training dataset. v2 also discloses L2 regularization and the ReLU-based SAE used in the existing multimodal analysis, and adds a link advertised as a complete results spreadsheet. That external resource's contents and availability were not assessed.

R1.justification: v2 adds SAEBench and MTEB citations and expands its comparison with Kantamneni's findings. Numerous other reference edits correct or consolidate bibliographic information for already cited work, without substantially changing the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: The main section structure is retained. Local additions include an experimental rationale, rewritten dataset description, expanded interpretation and limitations, and a new pooling appendix that shifts subsequent appendix labels. The action-prediction procedure is compressed into inline numbering.

P2.justification: The figure graphics and captions are retained, but Figure 6 and several appendix figures and tables move relative to surrounding prose. Table 5 becomes narrower with shorter numerical formatting, and the retrieved-feature table has different page breaks. There is no substantive visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.1 and the added implementation disclosures improve reproducibility, while Section 5.2 gives a more nuanced reading of Figure 5. However, the rewritten dataset description incorrectly suggests only three binary tasks despite the broader retained Table 2, and the new average-performance qualification remains beside the claim that Mean-Diff consistently lags behind. These documentation gains and new or unreconciled inconsistencies leave the net quality change uncertain.
